groups.label: What we read
statements: Events, and the people behind them, from the analytics you already run. We never write to it.
Recordings of sessions where something looked wrong. Never all of them.
Your code, read-only, so we can point at the right file. We never write code.

groups.label: What we set aside
statements: Visits from your own team, worked out from the email address that created this workspace.
Bots, automated browsers and coding agents.
When we are not sure whose visit is whose, we keep it. Setting aside a real customer would hide the very thing you are here to see.

groups.label: What a recording keeps
statements: What was pressed, and what it was labelled.
How many characters were typed — never the characters.
The address of each page as a tidied-up pattern, never the raw address with your customers' own details in it.
Who someone is, stored as a scrambled stand-in that cannot be turned back into a name or an address.
Below our confidence bar, the recording is withheld and we say so on the finding.

groups.label: What leaves this system
statements: Everything we send to your channel is checked for leftover personal details before it leaves.
Whether we were right or wrong goes into a record shared across customers. What your product is, who your users are, and anything they typed does not.

closing: Nothing here is a setting. There is nothing to switch on.
